ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, $ \angle ACB=90^\circ$, $AC=BC$, points D and E are on AB and AC respectively. CD and ED are connected, $ED=CD$, $\tan\angle ADE=\frac{1}{3}$, $BD=\sqrt{2}$. What is the length of $AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $EH \perp AB$ at H, and draw $DM \perp AC$ at M, and draw $DG \perp BC$ at G, \\
$\because \angle ACB=90^\circ$ and $AC=BC$, \\
$\therefore$ quadrilateral $CGDM$ is a rectangle, $\angle A=\angle B=45^\circ$, \\
$\therefore DG=CM$, \\
$\because BD=\sqrt{2}$, \\
$\therefore DG=BG=BD\cdot \sin 45^\circ=\sqrt{2}\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}=1$, \\
$\therefore CM=1$, \\
$\because DE=DC$ and $DM\perp AC$, \\
$\therefore EM=CM=1$, \\
$\because$ $\tan \angle ADE=\frac{1}{3}=\frac{EH}{DH}$, \\
Let $EH=x$, then $DH=3x$, \\
$\because \angle A=45^\circ$ and $EH\perp AH$, \\
$\therefore AH=EH=x$, \\
From $\sin A=\sin 45^\circ=\frac{AH}{AE}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, \\
$\therefore AE=\sqrt{2}x$, \\
Similarly: $\cos A=\cos 45^\circ=\frac{AC}{AB}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, \\
$\therefore AB=\sqrt{2}AC$, \\
$\therefore x+3x+\sqrt{2}=\sqrt{2}\left(\sqrt{2}x+2\right)$, \\
Solving gives: $x=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, \\
$\therefore AB=4x+\sqrt{2}=4\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+\sqrt{2}=\boxed{3\sqrt{2}}$

method.method_draft: From the image, read the configuration as a right isosceles triangle with C at the right-angle corner, A above C, B to the right of C, D on hypotenuse AB, E on vertical side AC, and segments CD and ED drawn. From the text, use AC=BC, BD=sqrt(2), ED=CD, and tan angle ADE=1/3. Let AC=BC=L, so AB=Lsqrt(2). Since D lies on AB and BD=sqrt(2), AD=(L-1)sqrt(2). Because the big triangle is 45-45-90, angle DAE=45 degrees. Let theta=angle ADE, so tan theta=1/3. Use sin theta=1/sqrt(10), cos theta=3/sqrt(10), and angle AED=135 degrees-theta. By the sine rule in triangle ADE, compute AE/AD=sin theta/sin(135 degrees-theta)=1/(2sqrt(2)), so AE=(L-1)/2. Also compute ED from the sine rule: ED=AD*sin45/sin(135 degrees-theta), giving ED^2=5(L-1)^2/4. Separately, in triangle BCD, use BC=L, BD=sqrt(2), and angle CBD=45 degrees to get CD^2=L^2+2-2L=(L-1)^2+1. Set ED^2=CD^2 and solve 5(L-1)^2/4=(L-1)^2+1, giving L=3, hence AB=3sqrt(2).

再推理：设 AC=BC=L。因为 ∠ACB=90° 且 AC=BC，所以 △ABC 是等腰直角三角形，AB=L√2，且 ∠A=∠B=45°。又因为 D 在 AB 上且 BD=√2，所以 AD=AB−BD=L√2−√2=(L−1)√2。
在 △ADE 中，E 在 AC 上，D 在 AB 上，所以 ∠DAE=45°。设 θ=∠ADE，已知 tan θ=1/3，因此 sin θ=1/√10，cos θ=3/√10。于是 ∠AED=180°−45°−θ=135°−θ。
计算 sin(135°−θ)=sin135°cosθ−cos135°sinθ=(√2/2)(3/√10)−(−√2/2)(1/√10)=2/√5。
由正弦定理，AE/AD=sinθ/sin(135°−θ)=(1/√10)/(2/√5)=1/(2√2)，所以 AE=(L−1)√2 · 1/(2√2)=(L−1)/2。
同理由正弦定理，ED/AD=sin45°/sin(135°−θ)=(√2/2)/(2/√5)=√10/4，因此 ED²=AD²·10/16=[(L−1)²·2]·10/16=5(L−1)²/4。
另一方面，在 △BCD 中，BC=L，BD=√2，且 ∠CBD=45°。由余弦定理，CD²=L²+2−2·L·√2·cos45°=L²+2−2L=(L−1)²+1。
已知 ED=CD，所以 5(L−1)²/4=(L−1)²+1。化简得 (L−1)²=4。由于 L>1，得 L−1=2，即 L=3。因此 AB=L√2=3√2。

raw_record.original_question: In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$ and $AC=BC$. Points $D$ and $E$ are on $AB$ and $AC$ respectively. Segments $CD$ and $ED$ are connected, with $ED=CD$, $\tan\angle ADE=\frac{1}{3}$, and $BD=\sqrt{2}$. Find the length of $AB$.
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw $EH \perp AB$ at $H$, $DM \perp AC$ at $M$, and $DG \perp BC$ at $G$. \\
$\because \angle ACB=90^\circ$ and $AC=BC$, \\
$\therefore$ quadrilateral $CGDM$ is a rectangle, and $\angle A=\angle B=45^\circ$. \\
$\therefore DG=CM$. \\
$\because BD=\sqrt{2}$, \\
$\therefore DG=BG=BD\cdot \sin 45^\circ=\sqrt{2}\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}=1$. \\
$\therefore CM=1$. \\
$\because DE=DC$ and $DM\perp AC$, \\
$\therefore EM=CM=1$. \\
$\because \tan \angle ADE=\frac{1}{3}=\frac{EH}{DH}$, \\
Let $EH=x$, then $DH=3x$. \\
$\because \angle A=45^\circ$ and $EH\perp AH$, \\
$\therefore AH=EH=x$. \\
From $\sin A=\sin 45^\circ=\frac{AH}{AE}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, \\
$\therefore AE=\sqrt{2}x$. \\
Similarly, $\cos A=\cos 45^\circ=\frac{AC}{AB}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, \\
$\therefore AB=\sqrt{2}AC$. \\
$\therefore x+3x+\sqrt{2}=\sqrt{2}(\sqrt{2}x+2)$. \\
Solving gives $x=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$. \\
$\therefore AB=4x+\sqrt{2}=4\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+\sqrt{2}=\boxed{3\sqrt{2}}$
